title: English Tenses and Time PDF Imported Question Bank
subject: English

questions.q: The best thing about your father is that he is always taking life with a positive attitude. Find out the error, if any.
options: The best thing about your father is that
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The simple present tense should be used for habitual actions. 'is always taking' should be replaced with 'always takes'.

questions.q: You are coming so late sometimes that it becomes very difficult for me to manage such a huge number of students. Find out the error, if any.
options: very difficult for me to manage
such a huge number of students.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For habitual actions indicated by 'sometimes', the simple present tense 'come' should be used instead of the present continuous 'are coming'.

questions.q: I go to the office only twice a week these days because I have got to supervise the on-going construction work at the different sites. Find out the error, if any.
options: I go to the office only
because I have got to supervise
the on-going construction work at the different sites.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The phrase 'these days' indicates a temporary situation, so the present continuous tense 'am going' should be used instead of the simple present 'go'.

questions.q: My mother goes out for a morning walk everyday because the doctor has advised her to do so if she really wants to get well soon. Find out the error, if any.
options: My mother goes out for a morning
to do so if she really wants to get well soon.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Everyday' (one word) is an adjective meaning commonplace. The adverbial phrase 'every day' (two words) should be used here to mean 'each day'.

questions.q: She is sneezing again, so I think she has a cold. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Sneezing is a momentary action. For a recently completed action with present relevance, the present perfect 'has sneezed' is more appropriate than the present continuous 'is sneezing'.

questions.q: I am not able to answer any of your questions because they did not give me enough information or data on it yet. Find out the error, if any.
options: I am not able to answer any of your
information or data on it yet.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The word 'yet' indicates an action continuing up to the present, requiring the present perfect tense 'have not given' instead of the simple past 'did not give'.

questions.q: You always come late and now I am not going to tolerate it any more. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: To express annoyance or irritation about a habitual action, the present continuous tense with 'always' ('are always coming') is used.

questions.q: People know that India can be a superpower only when they will work honestly and sincerely. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In adverbial clauses of time introduced by 'when', the simple present tense is used to refer to the future, not the future tense. 'will work' should be 'work'.

questions.q: Unless they come up and do not take up the responsibility of taking care of these pets, I cannot think of going away for any sort of pilgrimage. Find out the error, if any.
options: and do not take up the responsibility
of taking care of these pets,
I cannot think of going away for any sort of pilgrimage.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Unless' already carries a negative meaning ('if not'). Using 'do not' creates a double negative. It should be 'and take up the responsibility'.

questions.q: I am sorry to say that I cannot say anything unless I go through the entire documents. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The adjective 'entire' is singular and should modify a singular noun. 'documents' should be changed to 'document'.

questions.q: Unless you have the thorough analysis of the project, you can't say whether it can be finished within the given period of time or not. Find out the error, if any.
options: you can't say whether it can be
finished within the given period of time or not.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The definite article 'the' is inappropriate here as it refers to a non-specific analysis. It should be 'a thorough analysis'.

questions.q: You will have everything that you desire, provided that you work hard with some extra effort. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Provided that' is correctly followed by the simple present tense to indicate a condition for the future.

questions.q: He will call you up as soon as he will finish the work and move to another one. Find out the error, if any.
options: as soon as he will finish
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In time clauses introduced by 'as soon as', the simple present tense is used for future reference, not the future tense. 'will finish' should be 'finishes'.

questions.q: Everybody is talking about the latest movie produced by Vidhu Vinod Chopra, as it is bringing out the real face of Indian politics. Find out the error, if any.
options: about the latest movie produced by Vidhu Vinod Chopra,
the real face of Indian politics.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For a permanent characteristic or general truth revealed by the movie, the simple present tense 'brings out' is more appropriate than the present continuous 'is bringing out'.

questions.q: There are a number of books on History, which has focussed on the social scourge that has been coming down for ages in India. Find out the error, if any.
options: There are a number of books on History,
has been coming down for ages in India.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun 'which' refers to the plural noun 'books', so the verb must be plural. 'has focussed' should be 'have focussed'.

questions.q: Most of the newspapers today are saying that the common wealth game, 2010 has proved highly advantageous for the politicians and the bureaucrats who have been aspiring to be millionaires. Find out the error, if any.
options: Most of the newspapers today are saying that
the common wealth game, 2010 has proved
and the bureaucrats who have been aspiring to be millionaires.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The event is the 'Commonwealth Games' (plural), so the verb should be plural 'have proved'. Also, 'common wealth' should be 'Commonwealth'.

questions.q: A book which was published in 1980 said that Indira Gandhi belonged to a Muslim family in reality. Find out the error, if any.
options: to a Muslim family in reality.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When stating a universal truth or a permanent fact, the simple present tense is used even if the main verb is in the past. 'belonged' should be 'belongs'.

questions.q: I always admire the great man who said that one is wiser after an event. Find out the error, if any.
options: one is wiser after an event.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The tenses are used appropriately to express a general admiration and a reported universal truth.

questions.q: Now-a-days, film makers do not make that kind of movie which they made earlier. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: To express a past habit that is no longer true, 'used to make' is more appropriate than the simple past 'made'.

questions.q: When she asked me what I do these days, I started wondering if I should come out with the truth. Find out the error, if any.
options: if I should come out with the truth.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Due to the sequence of tenses, the reported speech should match the past tense of the reporting verb 'asked'. 'do' should be changed to 'was doing' or 'did'.

questions.q: When you will find out any solution to this problem you will become able to finalise the project. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In adverbial clauses of time introduced by 'when', the simple present tense is used for future reference. 'will find out' should be 'find out'.

questions.q: Whenever you are coming here, you bring a lot of sweets for me. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For habitual actions indicated by 'whenever', the simple present tense 'come' should be used instead of the present continuous 'are coming'.

questions.q: It is appearing to me that you are plotting against your friends and their parents. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The verb 'appear' (meaning 'seem') is a stative verb and is not typically used in the continuous form. It should be 'It appears to me'.

questions.q: The old man who is sitting in that room lived here for more than a month but he has never created any problem. Find out the error, if any.
options: The old man who is sitting in that room
a month but he has never created
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The action of living here started in the past and continues to the present (as he is still sitting in the room), so the present perfect 'has lived' should be used.

questions.q: A mysogynist is a person who is hating woman but a philogynist is a person who loves woman. Find out the error, if any.
options: but a philogynist is a person
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Hate' is a stative verb expressing a state of mind, not an action, so it should be in the simple present tense 'hates'. Also, 'women' (plural) is more appropriate than 'woman'.

questions.q: The secret of his good health lies in the fact that he is getting up before sunrise and has a two-mile walk every morning. Find out the error, if any.
options: health lies in the fact that
he is getting up before sunrise
and has a two- mile walk every morning.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: For a habitual daily routine ('every morning'), the simple present tense 'gets up' should be used instead of the present continuous 'is getting up'.

questions.q: Now-a-days he teaches physics becuase the teacher of physics has been absenting himself for a month. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Absent' is primarily an adjective or a transitive verb, but 'has been absent' is the correct stative construction. 'Has been absenting himself' is non-standard; 'has been absent' is correct.

questions.q: He seems to be happy because his parents had come from London to live with him. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The present perfect 'have come' should be used because the action of coming has a present result (they are now living with him, making him happy).

questions.q: "It is high time you are starting this work," my friend said to me. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: After the expression 'It is high time', the verb in the following clause must be in the simple past tense to indicate that something should be done immediately. 'are starting' should be 'started'.

questions.q: I have come to know that your father has died last week. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When a specific past time ('last week') is mentioned, the simple past tense must be used. 'has died' should be 'died'.

questions.q: Many of my friends wished to come here today but none of them arrived yet. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The word 'yet' indicates an action continuing up to the present, requiring the present perfect tense 'have arrived' instead of the simple past 'arrived'.

questions.q: She says that she will take her umbrella in case it will rain. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In conditional clauses introduced by 'in case', the simple present tense is used for future reference. 'will rain' should be 'rains'.

questions.q: I will let you know as soon as I will get any information about your promotion. Find out the error, if any.
options: as soon as I will get
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In time clauses introduced by 'as soon as', the simple present tense is used for future reference. 'will get' should be 'get'.

questions.q: When I will be thirty most of my friends will be above thirty five. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In adverbial clauses of time introduced by 'when', the simple present tense is used for future reference. 'will be' should be 'am'.

questions.q: This is, indeed, the first time in my life that I hear such an interesting story. Find out the error, if any.
options: the first time in my life that
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: After 'This is the first time', the present perfect tense is used. 'hear' should be 'have heard'.

questions.q: Before the alarm had stopped ringing Veera had pulled up the shade. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The action of the alarm stopping is a single completed event in the past, so the simple past 'stopped' should be used, not the past perfect.

questions.q: I have been knowing him for ten years but I don't know where he lives. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Know' is a stative verb and is not used in the continuous form. 'have been knowing' should be 'have known'.

questions.q: He uses to study at least till ten o'clock at night and then he goes to bed. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The correct phrase for a past habit is 'used to', not 'uses to'.

questions.q: If he had a few hours to spare, he would spend them in a public library. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is a correct second conditional structure (If + past simple, would + base verb). No error.

questions.q: All the flowers in his garden will surely die before the rains will fall. Find out the error, if any.
options: in his garden will surely die
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In time clauses introduced by 'before', the simple present tense is used for future reference. 'will fall' should be 'fall'.

questions.q: If I would have done this, I would have done wrong and would have disappointed many of my friends. Find out the error, if any.
options: If I would have done this,
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In third conditional 'if' clauses, the past perfect tense is used, not 'would have'. 'would have done' should be 'had done'.

questions.q: If she had told me that her husband never lived within his means, I would not have lent him the money. Find out the error, if any.
options: If she had told me that
within his means, I would not
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When stating a general truth or permanent habit within reported speech, the simple present tense is preferred. 'never lived' should be 'never lives'.

questions.q: I wish he saw you when you were living in England. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: To express a regret about a past event after 'I wish', the past perfect tense is used. 'saw' should be 'had seen'.

questions.q: The judge had not given any dicision until he had studied the case. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The action of not giving a decision is a simple past event preceding another past action. 'had not given' should be 'did not give'.

questions.q: I lived here since 1980, therefore I know everything about this city. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing to the present requires the present perfect tense. 'lived' should be 'have lived'.

questions.q: I have been working for this organisation for the last ten years. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the present perfect continuous tense to describe an action that started in the past and continues to the present.

questions.q: If we had Mohan in our team, we would have won the match against your team. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: This is a mixed conditional or third conditional error. To match 'would have won', the 'if' clause must be in the past perfect: 'If we had had Mohan'.

questions.q: Radha came to the meeting much later than I expect. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The main verb 'came' is in the past tense, so the subordinate clause should also be in the past tense. 'expect' should be 'expected'.

questions.q: If I was you I would have told the Chairman to keep his mouth shut. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In hypothetical 'if' clauses, 'were' is used for all persons. 'was' should be 'were'.

questions.q: I want you to pick up the box of eggs gently and kept it in the corner carefully. Find out the error, if any.
options: kept it in the corner carefully.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The verbs 'pick up' and 'keep' are parallel infinitives following 'want you to'. 'kept' should be 'keep'.

questions.q: The victim tried to tell us what has happened but his words were not audible. Find out the error, if any.
options: The victim tried to tell us
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The main verb 'tried' is in the past tense, so the reported event should be in the past perfect. 'has happened' should be 'had happened'.

questions.q: We got everything ready for all of them long before they arrived. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The action of getting everything ready happened before another past action ('arrived'), so the past perfect 'had got' or 'had gotten' should be used.

questions.q: She was with me uptil now, so don't rebuke her for getting late. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The phrase 'up till now' indicates a period continuing to the present, requiring the present perfect tense. 'was' should be 'has been'.

questions.q: I have been adoring her for the voice with which she is gifted. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Adore' is a stative verb expressing a state of mind and is not typically used in the continuous form. 'have been adoring' should be 'have adored'.

questions.q: Had he come even a moment earlier, he would have found me there. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is a correct inverted third conditional structure. No error.

questions.q: Many observations indicate that the number of the drug addicts is grew day by day. Find out the error, if any.
options: that the number of the drug
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The present continuous tense is required here to show an ongoing trend. 'is grew' is grammatically incorrect and should be 'is growing'.

questions.q: Newspapers told us about the events that happen all over the world. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Newspapers regularly report current events, so the simple present tense 'tell' should be used instead of the past tense 'told'.

questions.q: "Here is coming my friend!", said Manju when she was anxious. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: With verbs of motion like 'come' or 'go' used with 'here' or 'there', the simple present tense is used for immediate actions. 'is coming' should be 'comes'.

questions.q: He advised me to do as he did but I did not pay any attention to his advice. Find out the error, if any.
options: but I did not pay any attention
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The tenses are used appropriately to describe past advice and a past reaction.

questions.q: By this time next year he has had settled himself in London. Find out the error, if any.
options: By this time next year he
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The phrase 'By this time next year' requires the future perfect tense. 'has had' should be 'will have'.

questions.q: It is about time you have taken you children to shcool. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: After 'It is about time', the verb in the following clause must be in the simple past tense. 'have taken' should be 'took'.

questions.q: I had hoped that I would see you the other day, but unfortunately I fell ill. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence correctly uses the past perfect 'had hoped' to express an unfulfilled expectation in the past.

questions.q: The thief was caught after he has disposed of the stolen goods. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The action of disposing of the goods happened before the past action of being caught, so the past perfect 'had disposed' should be used.

questions.q: Sushma arrived here, did all the preparations and then has called on one of her intimate friends. Find out the error, if any.
options: on one of her intimate friends.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sequence of past actions requires the simple past tense. 'has called' should be 'called' to maintain parallelism with 'arrived' and 'did'.

questions.q: I could not recall what she has told me about her concern with Moti. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The main verb 'could not recall' is in the past tense, so the reported speech should be in the past perfect. 'has told' should be 'had told'.

questions.q: That two and two always made four cannot be doubted. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Universal truths or mathematical facts are always expressed in the simple present tense. 'made' should be 'makes'.

questions.q: Nobody knows when death will knock at his door. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The future tense is appropriately used in the noun clause.

questions.q: Dipu hopes to become an officer after he will complete his higher education. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In time clauses introduced by 'after', the simple present tense is used for future reference. 'will complete' should be 'completes'.

questions.q: Meenu along with her parents is going to Mumbai tonight because her eldest brother is ill there. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'Along with' does not change the singular subject 'Meenu', so 'is going' is correct.

questions.q: My friend said to me, "When have you come here?" Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When asking about a specific completed past action, the simple past tense is used. 'have' should be 'did'.

questions.q: He would not have done all this if he had not been instigated by his wife. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is a correct third conditional structure. No error.

questions.q: The teacher said to us that we should stay at home if it rains. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: Due to the sequence of tenses, the conditional clause should match the past tense of the reporting verb. 'rains' should be 'rained'.

questions.q: I have not seen him since twenty years and so I cannot say with certainty whether he is alive or dead. Find out the error, if any.
options: I have not seen him since twenty years
and so I cannot say with certainty
whether he is alive or dead.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time, while 'for' is used with a period of time. 'since twenty years' should be 'for twenty years'.

questions.q: When he did not find his cook in the kitchen he asked his wife where had he gone. Find out the error, if any.
options: When he did not find his cook in the kitchen
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In reported speech or indirect questions, the subject must precede the verb. 'where had he gone' should be 'where he had gone'.

questions.q: Although I am playing cricket for more than three years I have not been able to score a century. Find out the error, if any.
options: I have not been able to score a century
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing to the present requires the present perfect continuous tense. 'am playing' should be 'have been playing'.

questions.q: I do not know where could he have gone so early in the morning. Find out the error, if any.
options: I do not know where could he have gone
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In indirect questions, the subject must precede the auxiliary verb. 'where could he have gone' should be 'where he could have gone'.

questions.q: By the time we got our tickets and entered the cinema theatre, the show was already begun. Find out the error, if any.
options: we got our tickets and entered the cinema theatre,
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: An action completed before another past action requires the past perfect tense. 'was already begun' should be 'had already begun'.

questions.q: By the time we will get our tickets and enter the cinema theatre, the show will have already begun. Find out the error, if any.
options: we will get our tickets and enter the cinema theatre,
the show will have already begun.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. 'By the time' is correctly followed by the simple present for future reference, and the main clause uses the future perfect.

questions.q: Gowri told me his name after he left. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The action of leaving happened before the action of telling, so the past perfect tense should be used. 'left' should be 'had left'.

questions.q: we have been celebrating many festivals since centuries. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time, while 'for' is used with a period of time. 'since centuries' should be 'for centuries'.

questions.q: Old age and infirmity had began to catch up with him. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The past participle of 'begin' is 'begun', not 'began'. 'had began' should be 'had begun'.

questions.q: The passer-by told us where was the marriage hall and even led us to it. Find out the error, if any.
options: and even led us to it.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In indirect questions, the subject must precede the verb. 'where was the marriage hall' should be 'where the marriage hall was'.

questions.q: I have passed the examination two years ago. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When a specific past time ('two years ago') is mentioned, the simple past tense must be used. 'have passed' should be 'passed'.

questions.q: Since he joined this post, he did not take any bribe. Find out the error, if any.
options: this post, he did not take
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The word 'since' indicates a period from the past to the present, requiring the present perfect tense in the main clause. 'did not take' should be 'has not taken'.

questions.q: Perhaps you know that I have passed the examination in 1990. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: When a specific past time ('in 1990') is mentioned, the simple past tense must be used. 'have passed' should be 'passed'.

questions.q: He has read four plays written by Shakespeare by the end of his vacation. Find out the error, if any.
options: by the end of his vacation.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The phrase 'by the end of his vacation' refers to a future or past deadline. Assuming future, it should be 'will have read'. If past, 'had read'. 'has read' is incorrect.

questions.q: When they stole the money and where did they hide it?. Find out the error, if any.
options: and where did they hide it?.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: In indirect or embedded questions, the subject must precede the verb, and the auxiliary 'did' is not used. 'where did they hide it' should be 'where they hid it'.

questions.q: The teacher has took the responsibility. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The past participle of 'take' is 'taken', not 'took'. 'has took' should be 'has taken'.

questions.q: For time immemorial sea shells have been used by man in many ways. Find out the error, if any.
options: sea shells have been used by man
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The sentence is grammatically correct. The present perfect passive is appropriately used for an action continuing from the past to the present.

questions.q: The river is in spate and it has overflown its banks. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The past participle of 'overflow' is 'overflowed', not 'overflown'. 'has overflown' should be 'has overflowed'.

questions.q: The little boy had been waiting for his turn since a long time. Find out the error, if any.
options: had been waiting for his turn
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a specific point in time, while 'for' is used with a period of time. 'since a long time' should be 'for a long time'.

questions.q: This T.V. serial is going on for 3 years. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: An action starting in the past and continuing to the present requires the present perfect continuous tense. 'is going on' should be 'has been going on'.

questions.q: In the early years of the renaissance of Bharatanatyam, hereditary dancers have their own set of accompanists who lived with the dancers and travelled with them from place to place when they gave performances. Find out the error, if any.
options: In the early years of the renaissance of Bharatanatyam, hereditary dancers have their own set of accompanists
who lived with the dancers and travelled with them from place to place
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The context is in the past ('early years', 'lived', 'travelled'), so the verb should be in the past tense. 'have' should be 'had'.

questions.q: This is turned out to be one of our most successful projects and we have made quite a large profit from it. Find out the error, if any.
options: This is turned out to be
one of our most successful projects
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: 'Turn out' is an intransitive verb and does not take the passive voice. 'is turned out' should be 'has turned out'.

questions.q: He is given me a lot of documents to read before the presentation tomorrow. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The present perfect tense is required here. 'is given' should be 'has given'.

questions.q: Since the trip home was expensive I did not went home during the holidays. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: After the auxiliary 'did', the base form of the verb must be used. 'went' should be 'go'.

questions.q: As she is late for work yesterday she decided to skip breakfast and leave for office. Find out the error, if any.
questions.subject: English
questions.explanation: The time marker 'yesterday' requires the past tense. 'is late' should be 'was late'.

questions.q: As soon as the CEO entered the office, the union leaders approached him and report the matter to him. Find out the error, if any.
options: As soon as the CEO entered the office, the
and report the matter to him.
questions.subject: English
